content.title: About
content.content: Oysters Rockefeller is a classic American dish first served at the Delmonico’s restaurant in New York City in 1899. The oysters are baked in their shells with a rich sauce made from spinach, butter, Parmesan cheese, and aromatic herbs.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish is named after John D. Rockefeller, who allegedly asked for a richer sauce on his oysters.
The original recipe used only spinach, but over time cheese and breadcrumbs were added.
Oysters Rockefeller are often presented as the “king” of appetizers in seafood restaurants.
In the United States the dish is considered a symbol of luxury and appears on holiday menus.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Oysters provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Rich source of zinc
items.content: Zinc supports immune function and skin health.

items.title: Contains omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Polyunsaturated fats promote heart health and reduce inflammation.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Oysters are abundant in vitamin B12, important for the nervous system and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: They also provide iron, selenium and magnesium, which aid metabolism and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Seafood allergy
items.content: Oysters can trigger severe allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Risk of foodborne illness
items.content: Raw or undercooked oysters may contain Vibrio bacteria, so freshness and proper cooking are essential.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: The buttery, cheesy sauce can be salty; people with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Cholesterol
items.content: Oysters contain cholesterol, so those with elevated cholesterol levels should consume them in moderation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Oysters Rockefeller are served hot in their shells. Eat them directly from the shell with a small fork, or remove the meat and add it to salads or pasta.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh oysters refrigerated at 0‑4 °C, covered with a damp cloth. Use within 24 hours. Cooked oysters should be eaten the same day.
